Arthur DiBianca

Libertarian candidate for Railroad Commissioner, Texas

Retired computer programmer

Arthur DiBianca is the Libertarian Party nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against Republican Bo French and Democrat Jon Rosenthal. He is a retired computer programmer from Austin with no professional background in the oil and gas industry. He has run before for the Texas House, the Texas Senate and the U.S. Congress as a Libertarian.

Where DiBianca stands

Oil and gas regulation
Proposes regulating the oil and gas industry from a 'restitution-based' perspective: rather than setting rules in advance, ensure that property owners damaged by industry activity get prompt restitution.
Oil and gas regulation
Supports simplifying and cleaning up what he calls 100 years of Railroad Commission regulations.
Campaign priorities
Lists his top priorities as fully respecting landowners' property rights, giving property rights priority over industry interests, and improving transparency.
Role of the Railroad Commission
Says the commission's primary job is to secure the rights of its constituents, not to represent or promote the oil and gas industry, and that it should avoid 'regulatory capture'.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner, 2026
  • Retired computer programmer; previously worked for the Texas Department of Transportation (per Branch voter guide)
  • Lives in Austin; originally from San Antonio
  • Earlier Libertarian candidate for the Texas House (2012), Texas Senate District 21 (2022) and the U.S. Congress
  • Treasurer of the Travis County Libertarian Party since 2004 and staff assistant for the Libertarian National Committee since 2009 (per VoteYourViews)
